grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Reported speech: Statements
grammarPoints.rule: To report what someone said, use said (that) and move the verb one step into the past: is → was, don't → didn't, can → could.

chart.title: Reported speech: Statements

intro_examples.text: My dad said that the red beetle was really cool.
intro_examples.jp: 父は、その赤いカブトムシは本当にかっこいいと言いました。

intro_examples.text: My mom said she didn't like things that crawled on her head.
intro_examples.jp: 母は、頭をはうものは好きではないと言いました。

intro_examples.text: My teacher said that she could see the eyelash mite through the microscope.
intro_examples.jp: 先生は、顕微鏡でまつげダニが見えると言いました。

rows.pattern: “It is cool.” → He said that it was cool.
rows.example: My dad said that the red beetle was really cool.
rows.jp: 父はその赤いカブトムシは本当にかっこいいと言いました。

rows.pattern: “I don't like it.” → She said she didn't like it.
rows.example: My mom said she didn't like things that crawled on her head.
rows.jp: 母は頭をはうものは好きではないと言いました。

rows.pattern: “I can see it.” → She said she could see it.
rows.example: My teacher said that she could see the eyelash mite.
rows.jp: 先生はまつげダニが見えると言いました。

rows.pattern: pronouns change to match the new speaker
rows.example: Ben said that I was wrong.
rows.jp: ベンは私が間違っていると言いました。

rows.example: My mom said she didn't like things that crawled on her head.

chart.note_rule: Reported speech has no quotation marks. The words move one step back in time.
chart.note_exception: Pronouns change too: “You are wrong” becomes he said that I was wrong.
chart.note_exception_detail: That can be left out with no change in meaning: She said she could see it.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Order of adjectives
grammarPoints.shortName: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material
grammarPoints.rule: When you use more than one adjective before a noun, put them in a fixed order: opinion, size, age, shape, colour, origin, then material.
grammarPoints.pattern: opinion + size + age + shape + colour + origin + noun

chart.title: Order of adjectives

intro_examples.jp: かわいくて若い、しま模様の毛におおわれた生き物
小さくてとがった灰色の耳
変わった黒いオーストラリアの毛深いクモ

rows.jp: かわいくて若い、しま模様の毛におおわれた生き物
小さくてとがった灰色の耳

rows.example: a common red bug with a spotted back
rows.jp: 背中に斑点のあるふつうの赤い虫
変わった黒いオーストラリアの毛深いクモ
斑点のあるふつうのおとなの虫

chart.note_rule: English speakers follow this order without thinking. A wrong order sounds strange even though every word is correct.
chart.note_exception: Two or more adjectives before a noun usually take no commas in this pattern: a big red bug.
chart.note_exception_detail: Opinion adjectives (cute, strange, horrible, wonderful, amazing) always come first, before any fact adjective.

table.title: The order
notes: Opinion adjectives always come before fact adjectives.
Colour comes late, right before origin and the noun.
